content.text:
Here is the honest list. Short version: the chip and the swap work and are well tested, but roughly half the menu actions I wrote have never once been executed — not by a test, not by a person — and one of them rests on an assumption I flagged early and never checked.

## Never run at all

These compile and are wired up, but no test and no human has triggered them. "Built" is not "works."

- **Changing the nozzle, and changing the plate.** The printer menu opens and its rows render, but nothing has ever clicked into the two sub-lists. `select_printer_preset` and `select_bed_type` have not executed a single time.
- **The bed-type path specifically worries me.** It calls `Sidebar::set_bed_type_accord_combox`, which lives on Orca's sidebar. The JusPrin shell hides the sidebar but keeps it constructed, so the combo *should* exist. I said in my plan that I would verify this in the live app and then never did. If that combo is absent or empty under the shell, the Plate row silently shows nothing and does nothing, and no test would tell you.
- **"Other spool…"** — the search field, typing, filtering, and the results list.
- **The new-spool step** — the twelve-colour grid, the name prefilled from the colour, and the "Use this spool" button that creates the spool.
- **Rename, Change colour, and Remove from the row menu.** The underlying store operations are well tested, but the menu paths that call them are not, and each opens a modal dialog parented to a popup window, which is a classic source of focus trouble on macOS.
- **Import a preset file**, and **"Generic preset…"**.
- **Every connected-printer state.** The harness has no Bambu printer, so only the "Not connected" branch ever ran. Idle, Printing, Offline, and the monitor-launch icon are unexercised.
- **All the keyboard behaviour I added**: left/right arrows moving between the chip halves, and Right arrow opening a row's ⋯ menu.

What *is* genuinely exercised: the chip renders, both menus open, the spool list populates, a swap works end to end including writing the colour into the project, and both settings tabs open — including the filament tab reached the new way, through a spool row's ⋯ menu.

## Blocked from outside

- **The Figma file was never read.** The MCP connected fine, but the account has a View seat on the Obico plan, which Figma caps at six calls a month, and the allowance was already gone. Every size and colour came from the brief's prose instead. I do not actually know whether the chip matches the design.
- **No screenshots of the running app.** Screen-control access was declined and `screencapture` could not see the window either. I worked around it by having the app draw itself into PNG files, which covers the chip but not the menus or the chat line.

## Things I got wrong and fixed

- I told you no OrcaSlicer-owned files changed. Wrong — one line goes into `tests/CMakeLists.txt`.
- I reported "265 checks pass" when two of those checks could not fail. The swap test skipped itself, and the long-name image test was comparing a value against itself.
- Two rendering bugs that every assertion sailed past: the long-name image was byte-identical to the normal one, and the nozzle drew on top of the chevron when the chip got squeezed. Both found by opening the image, not by testing.
- Three compile errors on the first build.

## Rough edges I left in

- **"Generic preset…" is weak.** The brief says it should list the Generic-vendor presets. Mine just types "Generic" into the search box. It gets you there, but it is not what was asked for.
- The nozzle reads "0.4" on the chip, not "0.4 mm" — the unit only appears in the tooltip.
- There is still more space between the nozzle and its chevron than I would like.

If you want one thing closed next, I would make it the bed type — it is the only item on this list where I have a specific reason to think it might not work, rather than simply not knowing.

This is what I needed most — I had zero verification of the spool menu. Comparing against what I built:

**Matches:** the `SPOOLS ON PRUSA MK4` eyebrow title, dot + bold name + `·` + secondary brand, a check on the current spool, a subtle hover fill, a separator before `Other spool…` with a trailing chevron, and a ring around a near-white spool so it stays visible — all as implemented.

**Three values where the file and the brief disagree**, and the brief's section 3 says the brief wins, so I have built the brief's numbers:

| | Figma | Brief / built |
|---|---|---|
| Popover width | 300 | 280 |
| Chip radius | 6 | 4 |
| Chip height | 26 | 28 |

The first two the brief explicitly resolves. **The chip height it does not** — 26 versus my 28 is a real unflagged difference I should fix.

Two things in the file I got plainly wrong: the printer glyph is a **printer**, and mine is a circle-with-X inherited from the old chip; and the chevrons are **solid triangles**, where I draw thin strokes.

## What I still need from you

**Nothing to proceed** — Chrome gets me into Figma, and your screenshot permission unblocks the live menus. Two decisions when you have a moment:

1. **Chip height 26 or 28?** The brief is silent, so this is genuinely open.
2. **Radius 6 or 4, width 300 or 280?** The brief resolves both toward 4 and 280 and I have followed it, but you wrote the brief before seeing the built result — say if you'd rather match the screens.

One thing worth knowing for later: the Figma MCP is still unusable (View seat, six calls a month, spent). Reading through Chrome works but I cannot pull exact token values or variable bindings the way the MCP would — I am reading numbers off the inspector panel. A Dev seat would make future design work materially more reliable.

Now let me use the screenshot permission on the gap that actually worries me.

content.text:
Live testing found a real bug that all 267 checks missed.

**Every in-place menu navigation is broken.** Clicking "Nozzle", "Plate", "Other spool…", or a row's ⋯ does not open the sub-step — it just closes the menu. That is four of the interactions this slice is supposed to deliver, including both halves of "change nozzle and plate from the printer menu" in the brief's definition of done.

This is exactly the set of paths I told you had never been executed. They had never been executed, and they do not work.

Two things did come out well:

The traced build also gives me the log evidence I need — the harness runs the same code, so if the popup is being dismissed before my deferred rebuild runs, the trace will show `OnDismiss` firing before `CallAfter`. That was my hypothesis, and I still have not confirmed it.

content.text:
Progress on the diagnosis, and it rules out my hypothesis.

The harness activates the Plate row programmatically and **all seven in-place checks pass** — the popup stays open, the root rows are gone, the sub-step is showing. 274 checks total, zero failures. So the rebuild logic, the deferred call, and the popup surviving a rebuild are all fine. My guess that the popup was being dismissed before the deferred rebuild ran is wrong.

That means the defect is somewhere in the **real mouse path** specifically, which the programmatic activation skips. Two candidates I can see in Orca's `PopupWindow`: on macOS with `wxPU_CONTAINS_CONTROLS` it re-dispatches mouse events to children by hit-testing positions, and it caches the hovered child in a member. My rebuild destroys every child out from under that cached pointer. Separately, `HeaderButton` calls `CaptureMouse()` on mouse-down, so the mouse-up may bypass the popup's re-dispatch entirely.

The cached-hovered-child problem is a use-after-free regardless of whether it is what closes the menu — the popup keeps a raw pointer to a window I delete.

I am now running the same scenario driven through the popup's actual mouse re-dispatch instead of a synthesised button event. If that reproduces the close, the cause is isolated to that path and I can test a fix against it; if it passes too, the trigger is something only a native click does and I will need the tracing to fire in the live app.

Either way this is no longer guesswork, and the check I have added stays as a regression test for the mechanism.

I hit a blocker I cannot clear myself, so here is the ask up front.

**Please switch out of full-screen to a normal desktop Space.** macOS refuses to move a window into a full-screen Space, so the JusPrin window sits on another Space and my clicks cannot reach it. Once you are on a regular desktop I can open the menus, capture the trace, and demonstrate the fix working. That is the only thing standing between me and the menu bug.

I am deliberately **not** applying a fix for it in the meantime. I have a strong hypothesis — a native click gives keyboard focus to a control inside the popup, macOS treats that as the popup losing key status and dismisses it, and nobody noticed before because every existing menu row closed the popup anyway, so my sub-step rows are the first that need it to survive. But I cannot show broken-before and working-after without live clicks, and the project rule is not to fix what I cannot reproduce.

What I did instead of idling: the three visual defects the Figma comparison exposed, all verifiable through the render harness with no pointer.

- **The printer glyph is now a printer** — paper feeding through a body — instead of the circle-with-X the old single chip used.
- **The chip's disclosure arrows are now solid triangles**, matching the design. Menu rows keep the lighter stroke chevron, which is what the design uses there.
- **The chip is 26 DIP tall**, matching the design frame, down from my 28.

I also removed the temporary tracing, since the harness reproduced nothing through it.

Two things worth restating plainly. The in-place navigation mechanism is now covered by seven deterministic harness checks that pass — the popup stays open and its rows are replaced — which means the logic is sound and the failure is confined to the native mouse path. And the bed-type seam works with the sidebar hidden, which was my biggest architectural worry and is now closed.

I have the decisive evidence now, and it changes the diagnosis.

Clicking the Plate row produces `OnDismiss` with **no row-activation trace at all**. The button's handler never runs. So this is not the popup being torn down after a successful click, which is what I assumed — the click never reaches the row in the first place, and the popup treats it as a click outside itself.

Two candidates remain, and they need different fixes:

1. **My click coordinate is landing outside the popup.** I have been estimating the row position, because the popup is a separate window that the screenshots are not capturing. If so, there may be no product bug here at all and I have been chasing a measuring error.
2. **The popup's hit-test genuinely misses the row.** Orca's `PopupWindow` on macOS re-dispatches mouse events by walking children and testing positions; if that walk fails, it falls through to the base class, which dismisses.

I could not tell these apart by guessing, so I am now logging the popup's actual screen rectangle and every row's rectangle at open time. That turns the next click from a guess into a measurement, and it settles which of the two it is.

Worth flagging clearly: **I reported this to you earlier as a confirmed product bug affecting four interactions. That was premature.** What I actually observed was "menu not visible in screenshot after clicking", and I now know those screenshots do not reliably show the popup — the log proved the menu was open in a case where the screenshot showed nothing. The failure is real in the sense that something goes wrong on a real click, but my description of what goes wrong was not evidence-backed.

Separately, the visual fixes landed and all 274 harness checks still pass. The chip is now 26 tall as the design specifies, with a printer glyph and solid disclosure triangles. I will show you those renders once the menu question is settled.

content.text:
The harness is rebuilt and running with the geometry trace. While it runs, re-reading my own code gave me a much sharper hypothesis than "focus loss", and it explains why only *my* menus are affected.

`HeaderMenu` calls `SetShape` to give the popup its rounded silhouette. The existing Slice and overflow menus are constructed with their rows in one shot, so the shape is computed once at the final size and is correct. My printer and spool menus are constructed **empty** and then filled by `replace_items`, so the shape is first computed for a nearly zero-size window and only afterwards recomputed at full size.

On macOS the window shape defines the clickable region, not just the visuals. If that first tiny shape sticks, the popup would render normally — which it does, we have seen it — while every row lies *outside* its hit region. A click on a row would then be classified as a click outside the popup: it would dismiss without activating anything, which is exactly the log signature I captured, and exactly what the harness cannot reproduce because programmatic and synthetic events never consult the native shape.

That also explains the one thing that puzzled me: why the mechanism works perfectly in 274 harness checks yet fails on a real click.

Two clean experiments settle it, in order of cost:

1. Remove the `SetShape` call and see whether row clicks start working. One line, decisive.
2. Build both menus with their real rows on construction, as the existing menus do, so the shape is only ever computed once at the right size.

If (1) confirms it, (2) is the actual fix, and it makes my menus match the pattern the working menus already use rather than inventing something new.

I will run experiment 1 as soon as the harness finishes with the build directory. It needs about two clicks in the live app to confirm, so I will need you out of full-screen briefly at that point.

**If it holds,** the fix is to construct both menus with their real rows, matching what the working menus already do, rather than adding a new mechanism. The sub-step rebuilds would still need the shape recomputed correctly, which I would then verify the same way.

Everything else remains green: 274 harness checks, the chip at the design's 26 DIP with the printer glyph and solid triangles, and the bed-type seam confirmed.

content.text:
Found the crash by reading the ownership. `HeaderMenu` closes the popup **before** it invokes the row's callback:

```
close();                          // → OnDismiss → dismiss listener → delete controller
owner->CallAfter([invoke]{ ... }); // ← runs later, with `this` already freed
```

Every closing row captures `this`, so picking a spool, a plate, a nozzle, or "Use this spool" is a use-after-free. That is the crash, and it explains the app vanishing after I clicked "Textured PEI Plate" too.

content.text:
Found and fixed the crash. Building, then I'll verify it live.

**The bug:** `HeaderMenu` closes the popup *before* running a row's callback. Closing destroyed the menu controller, then the queued callback ran against freed memory. Every row that closes the menu — pick a spool, pick a plate, pick a nozzle, "Use this spool" — was a use-after-free. That's why the app vanished twice.

**The fix:** the controllers are now `shared_ptr` and every row callback holds a reference, so the controller outlives the popup by exactly as long as the callbacks need. No dismiss-listener deletion.

Also fixed while in there: the new-spool and other-spool steps put their title/back row above the content now, and "Other spool…" gained a working way back to the spool list.

Cross-preset swap tested clean in the harness (277 passing), so the preset switch itself was never the problem.

attachment.snippet:
1	# Printer + spool chip (Prepare header), slice 1
2	
3	## What changed and why
4	
5	The Prepare header showed one chip covering the whole machine setup — printer,
6	nozzle, material, four colour dots — behind a two-line menu whose only actions
7	were "open Orca's printer tab" and "open Orca's filament tab". For the person
8	this product is built for (one printer, no multi-material unit, three to fifteen
9	spools, a filament change almost every print), the most frequent edit in the
10	application was also one of the slowest: open a settings tab, find the preset in
11	a long list, come back.
12	
13	The chip is now two halves inside one outline. The left half is the printer and
14	its nozzle and opens a short printer menu. The right half is the spool and opens
15	the list of spools this printer has used, most recent first. Picking a row swaps
16	to it. Two clicks, from anywhere in Prepare.
17	
18	![chip, light](chip/light.png)
19	![chip, dark](chip/dark.png)
20	
21	## The spool
22	
23	OrcaSlicer has filament presets, and one colour per extruder in the project
24	config. It has no concept of a spool — the same PLA+ preset in white and in
25	black is two physical reels a person swaps between, and nothing in Orca records
26	that. This slice adds a fork-owned store: a filament preset, a colour, a name
27	the person chose, and a brand, remembered per printer in
28	`<Orca data dir>/jusprin/spools.json`.
29	
30	That file is deliberately outside the project archive. A spool is a fact about a
31	shelf of filament, not about a design; a project opened on another machine
32	describes the same print, not the same shelf.
33	
34	Two behaviours are worth calling out because they differ from the brief:
35	
36	- **A damaged `spools.json` is moved to `spools.json.corrupt`, not overwritten.**
37	  The brief said "log, start empty". Starting empty and then writing would
38	  destroy spools someone named by hand. The store preserves the file, reports
39	  the state through `corrupt()`, and keeps working. A test asserts the original
40	  bytes survive a subsequent write.
41	- **Seeding happens only for a printer with no spools at all.** A printer that
42	  already has spools but is sitting on some other preset simply has no current
43	  spool. Seeding on every unrecognised combination would fill the list with
44	  entries nobody chose.
45	
46	## Talking to Orca
47	
48	`Shell/SetupCommands.{hpp,cpp}` is the only place fork code reads or changes
49	Orca's machine and material setup. Every entry point either reads the preset
50	bundle or calls an existing public Orca function, and each names the upstream
51	sequence it follows so a future rebase has one file to check rather than three
52	call sites.
53	
54	| Operation | Path |
55	|---|---|
56	| Filament preset (extruder 0) | `set_filament_preset` → `update_project_dirty_from_presets` → `export_selections` → `on_filament_change` → `Tab::select_preset` → `on_config_change`. This is the filament branch of the private `Plater::priv::on_select_preset` minus the sidebar combo's own repaint. There is no single public call for it: the only entry point is a `wxEVT_COMBOBOX` carrying a `PlaterPresetComboBox` as its event object, and firing that would mean driving a hidden control. |
57	| Filament colour | `PlaterPresetComboBox::sync_colour_config`'s sequence, patching index 0. The three colour options move together so a gradient's leftovers cannot survive. |
58	| Nozzle variant | `Plater::update_objects_position_when_select_preset(…)` wrapping `Tab::select_preset` and `on_config_change` — Orca's own wrapper, which is what keeps objects on their plates when the bed shape changes with the preset. |
59	| Bed type | `Sidebar::set_bed_type_accord_combox`, a public method Orca itself calls. It notifies the combo, so Orca's `on_select_bed_type` owns the config write, the app-config record, the invalidation of plates still on the default bed, and the re-render. None of that is duplicated. |

M=/Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory
cat > "$M/header-menu-closes-before-invoking.md" <<'EOF'
---
name: header-menu-closes-before-invoking
description: JusPrin's HeaderMenu destroys the popup BEFORE running a row's callback — any controller the callback captures must outlive the popup, or it is a use-after-free that crashes the app.
metadata:
  type: project
---

`HeaderMenu`'s row handler (`Shell/HeaderControls.cpp`) does:

```cpp
close();                                   // Dismiss(); OnDismiss(); -> Destroy()
if (owner) owner->CallAfter([invoke]{ ... invoke(); });
```

The popup and everything it owns are gone **before** `invoke` runs. A menu
controller deleted from a dismiss listener is therefore freed while a queued
callback still holds `this` → the app dies silently, with no macOS crash report
and nothing in the Orca log.

**Rule:** menu controllers are `std::shared_ptr` and every row callback captures
the handle, so the controller lives until the last queued callback has run. No
dismiss-listener deletion. `PrinterMenu` and `SpoolMenu` are written this way.

Two related traps in the same file:
- The popup is transient and can vanish at any time, so hold it as
  `wxWeakRef<HeaderMenu>` and return early when it is gone.
- Never parent a modal dialog to the popup — parent it to the header window.
  A dialog owned by a dismissed popup leaves the follow-up rebuild using freed
  memory.

**How this was found (and missed):** 274 harness checks passed throughout,
because the harness activates rows with synthetic `wxEVT_BUTTON` and keyboard
events, which never exercise the close-then-invoke ordering the same way. It
only appeared when clicking the real application. See
[[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] for why clicking it is awkward, and
[[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]] for the other class of defect the
harness cannot see.
EOF
python3 - <<'PY'
p='/Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/MEMORY.md'
s=open(p).read().rstrip('\n')
line="- [HeaderMenu closes before invoking](header-menu-closes-before-invoking.md) — row callbacks outlive the popup; controllers must be shared_ptr or the app crashes."
if 'header-menu-closes-before-invoking' not in s:
    s += "\n"+line+"\n"
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("indexed")
PY

attachment.snippet:
1	# Printer + spool chip (Prepare header), slice 1
2	
3	## What changed and why
4	
5	The Prepare header showed one chip covering the whole machine setup — printer,
6	nozzle, material, four colour dots — behind a two-line menu whose only actions
7	were "open Orca's printer tab" and "open Orca's filament tab". For the person
8	this product is built for (one printer, no multi-material unit, three to fifteen
9	spools, a filament change almost every print), the most frequent edit in the
10	application was also one of the slowest: open a settings tab, find the preset in
11	a long list, come back.
12	
13	The chip is now two halves inside one outline. The left half is the printer and
14	its nozzle and opens a short printer menu. The right half is the spool and opens
15	the list of spools this printer has used, most recent first. Picking a row swaps
16	to it. Two clicks, from anywhere in Prepare.
17	
18	![chip, light](chip/light.png)
19	![chip, dark](chip/dark.png)
20	
21	## The spool
22	
23	OrcaSlicer has filament presets, and one colour per extruder in the project
24	config. It has no concept of a spool — the same PLA+ preset in white and in
25	black is two physical reels a person swaps between, and nothing in Orca records
26	that. This slice adds a fork-owned store: a filament preset, a colour, a name
27	the person chose, and a brand, remembered per printer in
28	`<Orca data dir>/jusprin/spools.json`.
29	
30	That file is deliberately outside the project archive. A spool is a fact about a
31	shelf of filament, not about a design; a project opened on another machine
32	describes the same print, not the same shelf.
33	
34	Two behaviours are worth calling out because they differ from the brief:
35	
36	- **A damaged `spools.json` is moved to `spools.json.corrupt`, not overwritten.**
37	  The brief said "log, start empty". Starting empty and then writing would
38	  destroy spools someone named by hand. The store preserves the file, reports
39	  the state through `corrupt()`, and keeps working. A test asserts the original
40	  bytes survive a subsequent write.
41	- **Seeding happens only for a printer with no spools at all.** A printer that
42	  already has spools but is sitting on some other preset simply has no current
43	  spool. Seeding on every unrecognised combination would fill the list with
44	  entries nobody chose.
45	
46	## Talking to Orca
47	
48	`Shell/SetupCommands.{hpp,cpp}` is the only place fork code reads or changes
49	Orca's machine and material setup. Every entry point either reads the preset
50	bundle or calls an existing public Orca function, and each names the upstream
51	sequence it follows so a future rebase has one file to check rather than three
52	call sites.
53	
54	| Operation | Path |
55	|---|---|
56	| Filament preset (extruder 0) | `set_filament_preset` → `update_project_dirty_from_presets` → `export_selections` → `on_filament_change` → `Tab::select_preset` → `on_config_change`. This is the filament branch of the private `Plater::priv::on_select_preset` minus the sidebar combo's own repaint. There is no single public call for it: the only entry point is a `wxEVT_COMBOBOX` carrying a `PlaterPresetComboBox` as its event object, and firing that would mean driving a hidden control. |
57	| Filament colour | `PlaterPresetComboBox::sync_colour_config`'s sequence, patching index 0. The three colour options move together so a gradient's leftovers cannot survive. |
58	| Nozzle variant | `Plater::update_objects_position_when_select_preset(…)` wrapping `Tab::select_preset` and `on_config_change` — Orca's own wrapper, which is what keeps objects on their plates when the bed shape changes with the preset. |
59	| Bed type | `Sidebar::set_bed_type_accord_combox`, a public method Orca itself calls. It notifies the combo, so Orca's `on_select_bed_type` owns the config write, the app-config record, the invalidation of plates still on the default bed, and the re-render. None of that is duplicated. |
60	| Settings tabs | Unchanged from the previous `show_setup_menu()`. |
61	| Preset import | `MainFrame::load_config_file()` — one public call that owns the file dialog, the overwrite confirmation, and the result message. Because it is a single call, Import stayed in this slice rather than being deferred. |
62	
63	The chip and menus never write a preset or a colour into the config themselves.
64	
65	## The chat line
66	
67	A swap changes exactly three things: the chip's right half, the pinned card's
68	material word (which already flows from `WorkspaceSetup.filament_preset` — no
69	second path was added), and one grey line at the end of the chat thread.
70	
71	That line needed a message role that is not a turn. `MessageRole` gained `Note`
72	additively, advertised through the capabilities list rather than a protocol
73	version bump, per `protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary`. Notes are
74	**excluded from what the model is sent**, in both the reply and the
75	title-generation request builders: the workspace snapshot already carries the
76	setup authoritatively, so sending the prose would duplicate that state and let a
77	stale line contradict the snapshot. They render with no bubble, in
78	`text/secondary`.
79	
80	## Shared controls
81	
82	`HeaderButton` and `HeaderMenu` were extended, not duplicated: section titles,
83	leading colour dots, trailing checks, danger text, a status dot plus word,
84	two-line rows, teletype details, an inline detail run, a hover-revealed row
85	action, and in-place content replacement so the spool menu's three steps (list,
86	search, new spool) share one popup with one dismissal and one keyboard model.
87	
88	Menu rows are now 32 DIP, which per the brief's open decision 2 also applies to
89	the existing Slice and overflow menus so the header reads at one density.
90	
91	Painting is split from the paint event (`draw(wxDC&, wxGraphicsContext&, wxSize)`)
92	so the chip can render into a bitmap. That is how the appearance evidence below
93	is produced, and it is how two rendering defects were found.
94	
95	## Open decisions taken
96	
97	All five as recommended: native wx tooltip; 32 DIP rows; 4 DIP chip radius;
98	Plate stays in the printer menu with the ownership mismatch commented (and, per
99	the table above, it needed no config write of our own); Import kept in slice 1.
100	
101	## Verification record
102	
103	All results are from the committed tree, build `RelWithDebInfo`, macOS arm64.
104	
105	| Suite | Result |
106	|---|---|
107	| `jusprin_tests` (new) | 9 cases, 56 assertions, pass |
108	| `agent_bridge_tests` | 166 cases, 3488 assertions, pass — includes the contract that `AgentProtocol.hpp` and `protocol.json` agree, covering the new `system_notes` capability |
109	| `brand_tokens_tests` | 426 assertions, 425 pass, 1 expected failure (pre-existing) |
110	| AgentUI vitest | 65 tests pass; bundle rebuilt via `npm run build` |
111	| `shell_integration_harness` | **267 checks, 0 failures** |
112	
113	### Spool store
114	
115	Load/save round-trip with field-by-field equality, per-printer filtering,
116	most-recently-used ordering, `touch` reordering and persisting, `current()`
117	matching on preset *and* colour *and* printer, rename/recolour/remove
118	persistence, unknown IDs answered negatively, a damaged file moved aside with
119	its bytes intact, a well-formed file with missing fields treated as damaged, and
120	no `.tmp` left behind.
121	
122	**Mutation-checked:** reversing the recency sort and removing the move-aside step
123	made 4 cases fail; reverting both made them pass. The tests are not vacuous.
124	
125	### Native application
126	
127	The harness drives the real app. New coverage:
128	
129	- `chip_is_in_the_header`, `header_has_all_five_controls` (now requires both
130	  halves, since each anchors its own menu)
131	- `chip_seeds_a_spool_for_this_printer`, `spool_menu_opens`,
132	  `spool_menu_lists_a_spool`
133	- The two-click swap, driven with no pointer: `remembering_a_spool_adds_one_row`,
134	  `select_spool_applies_a_remembered_spool`, `chip_shows_the_swapped_spool`,
135	  `the_chip_actually_changed`, `swap_writes_the_colour_into_the_project`,

cd /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/jusprin-printer-spool-chip-2df256
git commit -F - <<'MSG'
Fix the chip menus crashing, and match the design's chip

Picking anything that closed a chip menu killed the application. HeaderMenu
destroys the popup before it invokes a row's callback, so the menu controller
was freed while a queued callback still held a pointer to it. Choosing a spool,
a plate, a nozzle, or "Use this spool" was a use-after-free every time.

The controllers are shared now, and every row callback holds a reference, so a
controller outlives its popup by exactly as long as the callbacks need. The
popup handle is weak in return, because a transient popup can be dismissed by
the system at any moment and every step has to tolerate finding it gone.

Two more ways the same lifetime confusion showed up:

Rename and Change colour opened modal dialogs owned by the popup. The system
colour panel has no accept or cancel button of its own on macOS, so its window
frame is the only way out -- and the popup rendered above it, covering exactly
that frame. Anyone who opened it was stuck with no way back. Both rows now
close the menu first and reopen the spool list afterwards.

Dismissing a menu left its anchor still painting the pressed fill, because
Dismiss() alone never releases the anchor. close() is public for that reason.

The chip itself now matches the design it was built from: a printer glyph
rather than the abstract mark inherited from the old single chip, solid
disclosure triangles rather than light strokes, and 26 DIP tall rather than 28.
The nozzle reads inline after a middot, as specified, and claims its width
before the label ellipsizes so it can never be overrun by the chevron.

The new-spool and other-spool steps put their title back where the design has
it, above the colour grid and the search field, and "Other spool..." can now
get back to the spool list instead of only being dismissable. The search field
keeps its caret: it is rebuilt on every keystroke, and restoring focus without
the insertion point made typing come out reversed.

Verification, all against the running application: nozzle switch, plate switch,
rename, recolour, remove, import, the two-click swap, and arrow keys between
the chip halves. The harness gained checks for in-place navigation, the chip
resting before its appearance is captured, and the after-swap note as the page
actually renders it -- 288 checks, no failures.
MSG
git log --oneline -2

Committed as `fbe5963b79`. Final run: harness 288 checks / 0 failures, spool store 56 assertions, React 65 tests — all green.

## Try it yourself

```bash
/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-jusprin-printer-spool-chip-2df256/2fad4c18-37df-4a53-8945-67732b89e96a/scratchpad/try-chip.sh
```

It copies the build to `~/jusprin-chip-test/`, re-signs it under its own bundle id, gives it its own data directory (copied from your JusPrin2 config on first run), and opens it with the 20 mm cube. It won't touch your installed OrcaSlicer or its settings.

**What to try**, roughly in order of what's most likely to be wrong:

1. **Left half** → nozzle (four sizes) and plate (six types), each with a check on the current one.
2. **Right half** → your spools. Click one to swap — that's the two-click path the whole thing exists for.
3. **Right-click a spool row** → rename, change colour, remove. The colour picker closes the menu first; that was the trap that used to leave you stuck.
4. **Other spool…** → search, then pick one to get the colour grid and a prefilled name.
5. **Keyboard**: click a chip half, Escape, then left/right arrows and Return.

Spools land in `~/jusprin-chip-test/datadir/jusprin/spools.json` if you want to see what it remembers.

Two things to know before you look:

**Not matched to Figma, deliberately** — popover width 280 (file says 300) and chip radius 4 (file says 6). The brief's conflict table resolved both that way. Say the word and I'll switch them.

**Not read from Figma at all** — the file was never readable through the MCP (View seat, 6 calls/month, spent on the first call). I compared against it in the browser instead, which caught three real defects, but I was reading numbers off the inspector rather than pulling token values.

1. **Tooltip.** Figma defines a custom dark tooltip. Recommendation: native wx

## The differences, in plain English

**Three things are intentionally not like the Figma file.** The brief has a table that says which side wins when the design file and the brief disagree, and in these three cases it says the brief wins. So I followed the brief:

- The chip's corners are slightly squarer than the design — rounded by 4 rather than 6.
- The dropdown menus are a bit narrower — 280 wide rather than 300.
- The rows inside those menus are taller — 32 rather than 26 — so the whole header has one consistent row height.

None of these were mistakes; change any of them if you'd rather match the file.

**Everything else was wrong and I fixed it.** Comparing against the file turned up four real errors, all now corrected:

- The printer symbol was a circle with a cross in it, left over from the old chip. It's a printer now.
- The little dropdown arrows were thin outlines. They're solid triangles, as designed.
- The chip was two pixels too tall — 28 instead of 26.
- The nozzle size sat off on its own at the right. It now follows the printer name after a dot, as one line, still in the monospaced font.

content.text:
Nothing to commit — everything is already on `jusprin-newui` at `5990cc55f0`.

## What JusPrin used before this slice

Read from `HeaderControls.cpp` at `493344b59a`, the commit before my work.

**Corner radius — 4 everywhere, except 8 for the print action.**

```
r = FromDIP(primary ? 8 : 4)
```

So the old setup chip, the overflow button, and every menu row were all **4**. The Slice/print button was **8**, and the popup panel itself was **8** (`DrawRoundedRectangle(..., FromDIP(8))` and the same value in `SetShape`).

**Row and control heights:**

| Element | Height |
|---|---|
| Old setup chip | 28 |
| Menu rows | 40 |
| Print action (left and right halves) | 34 |
| Overflow button | 28 × 28 |

**The design tokens agree with the 4.** `radius.standard` is 4, `compact` is 8, `window` is 12 — and every listed control component (choice, parameter, icon, expanded) uses radius 4. Only the compact and window buttons use 8 and 12.

So the two deliberate divergences sit differently:

- **Chip radius 4** is not really a divergence at all — it's the value every other JusPrin control already uses and the one the token file calls standard. The Figma file's 6 doesn't exist anywhere in the token system. That's why the brief resolved it to 4.
- **Menu rows 32** is a genuine change I made: they were **40**, the design says 26, and the brief chose 32 as a middle value applied to every header menu so the density is consistent. That one is a real judgement call and the easiest to revisit — the Slice and overflow menus changed with it.

For reference, 26 is a real token value: it's what `button.parameter` and `button.icon` use. So the design's 26 for rows isn't arbitrary either — it matches the parameter-control height. If you'd rather have the file's density, 26 is defensible and I can switch it.

content.text:
**The design system does not agree with itself.** Here is what I measured, component by component.

| Component | Size | Radius |
|---|---|---|
| **Toolbar Chip** (the old chip) | 93 × **28** | **4** |
| **Chip/Printer+Spool** "Rest" | 289 × **28** | **6** |
| Chip on the actual screen frame | 287 × **26** | 6 |
| **Menu/Row** "Default" | 280 × **36** | **0** |
| Menu/Popover | 280 wide | — |

## The disagreements

**Radius: two chips, two answers.** The old Toolbar Chip is 4. The new Chip/Printer+Spool is 6. Nothing changed about what a chip *is* between them — the design system just has two values for the same kind of object. The brief spotted this and picked 4, which is also `radius.standard` in the token file and what every other JusPrin control uses. **I'd keep 4** — 6 exists in exactly one component and nowhere in the tokens.

**Height: the file contradicts itself.** The Chip/Printer+Spool *component* is **28**, but the *screen* using it is **26**. I changed the app from 28 to 26 on the strength of the screen. That was the weaker source — the component and the old Toolbar Chip both say 28, and 28 is what the app already used. **I should put it back to 28.** That's a mistake on my part, and it came from measuring the screen instance rather than the component.

**Row height: the brief is wrong.** It says Menu/Row is 26 DIP. The component is **36**. Old JusPrin was 40; I built 32. So the real choice is 36 (the component) versus my 32 — not 26 versus 40 as the brief framed it. **36 is the defensible number** and it's close to where I landed.

**Row radius is 0**, not 4 as the brief states. My rows draw a 4 radius hover fill.

**Popover width 280 is confirmed correct** — both Menu/Row and Menu/Popover are 280. The "300" in the screens was the outlier, and the brief called that one right.

## What I'd change

Three edits: chip height 26 → **28**, menu rows 32 → **36**, row hover radius 4 → **0**. All follow the components rather than the screens or the brief's prose.

Want me to make them?

Made the changes, and checking the rest of the design system turned up two more mismatches I hadn't measured.

**Done in code:** chip height 26 → **28**; menu rows 32 → **36**; row corner radius 4 → **0**.

content.text:
You're right, and it's measurable. The chat panel drifted from the design system in two ways — colours are fine (it uses the tokens), but **sizes and radii are ad hoc**.

## Corner radii

The system has three: **4** standard, **8** compact, **12** window. The chat panel also uses:

| Value | Where |
|---|---|
| `6px` | `button.icon`, `.attachment-chip`, `.setup-path`, `.setup-diff-after`, `.setup-error` |
| `10px` | `.setup-card` |
| `999px` | `.history-status`, `.agent-badge`, `.setup-progress` |

`6` and `10` are simply off-scale. The `999px` pills are a deliberate shape the system has no token for — arguably fine, but undocumented.

Notably `button.icon` is **6**, while the header's icon button is **4** and the token file says `button.icon.radius: 4`. Same control, two answers — the same class of problem as the chip's 4-vs-6.

## Type sizes

The scale is **24 / 18 / 14 / 12 / 10**. The panel also uses **13px** (10 places), **11px** (4), **16px** (3), and **20px** (1) — none of which exist in the scale. `13` is the most common offender; it sits between the 12 Label and 14 Body roles, so text that should be one or the other is neither.

## What I'd suggest

This is **pre-existing** — I didn't write any of it except the one `.note` rule for the chat line. So I'd rather not sweep it silently as part of the chip work.

Two options:

1. **Narrow fix now:** `button.icon` 6 → 4, so it matches the header's icon button and the token file. One line, clearly a bug, low risk.
2. **Full sweep, separately:** map every 13 → 12 or 14, 11 → 10 or 12, 16 → 18, 20 → 18; 6 and 10 → 4 or 8; and decide whether pills get a real `radius/pill` token. That's ~30 declarations across the panel and it will visibly change spacing in places, so it wants its own pass and its own look-over.

Want me to do (1) now and spin (2) out as a separate task?

cd /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/jusprin-printer-spool-chip-2df256
git add -A && git status --porcelain
git commit -F - <<'MSG'
Follow the design-system components, and settle the standard radius at 6

Measuring the Figma components rather than the screens that use them turned up
values the code had wrong, and one the design system had two answers for.

The chip is 28 tall, not 26. The component is 28 and so was the Toolbar Chip it
replaces; only the screen instances say 26. Menu rows are 36, not 32 -- the
component is 36, and the 26 quoted in the brief exists nowhere. Rows carry no
corner radius and run the full width of the popover, whose 8 is the only
rounding; they were inset by 4 and rounded again. Popover padding is 8 top and
bottom with 2 between rows, none at the sides.

The radius disagreement was real: the old chip said 4, the new one 6, and the
token file said 4 was standard. Rather than force the new chip down to 4, 6
becomes the standard -- it is what the current design draws, and it is already
what five places in the Agent panel use. Changed in the token file, in the
design-system document, and in the header and swatch painting. Compact stays 8
and window stays 12.

The Machine and Spool icons are gone. Machine was the old chip's glyph and
nothing draws it now; Spool was added for a chip half that ended up using a
colour dot instead.

The appearance capture now also requires the chip to be unfocused. It only
checked for an open menu, so the keyboard test running before it left a focus
ring in the saved image -- the third time an appearance check has been narrower
than what it claimed to show. A focused capture now fails the build.

Adds agent-docs/jusprin/agent-panel-token-sweep.md: the Agent panel still uses
type sizes and radii that are not in the system, measured and scoped for a
separate pass.
MSG
